summary: Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Hare School, Presidency University, under Alexander Duff, and at Bishop's College, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School (~1829–1831) and Bishop's College (1852).

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at University College Thiruvananthapuram and University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He held key posts at Panjab University, Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, and Adyar Library.

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi (1918–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University, Honorary Director of the Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Research Foundation, and Upakulapati at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha (attested 1997).

Krishnanath Chatterjee was an Indologist. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He has held positions at Jawaharlal Nehru University as Professor (attested 2009) and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).
Kristi Wiley is an Indologist who held positions at the University of California, Berkeley, serving as a research assistant to the Translation Project (attested 1984) and continuing there in 1997.

Kristin Johnston Largen specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Wartburg Theological Seminary, United Lutheran Seminary as Professor of Systematic Theology (attested 2018), and Gettysburg College (attested 2018).

Kristin Scheible is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. She is the Thomas Lamb Eliot Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College.

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She studied for her Ph.D. at Lund University, where she also worked as an editor in 2005, and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) specialized in sinology and religious studies. He studied at École du Louvre, INALCO, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. His main appointments included EFEO, EPHE (1972–2002), CNRS, Collège de France, Leiden University, and Fuzhou University.

Kristóf Szitár works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Uppsala, CEU, Tübingen, and the University of Lausanne, holding research and teaching appointments at Lausanne, Heidelberg, Yale, and Yerevan State University.

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA and later served as a research fellow (~2009) at Eötvös Loránd University.
Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Calcutta (attested 1966), where she studied under Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Calcutta, Presidency, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under Ganganatha Jha. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1924–1956) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1900–1902) and held positions in the Chamba State Department of Education (~1902–1908) and Visva-Bharati University from 1908, serving as Adhyaksha (1953–1954).
Kumar Shrestha is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held a post at the National Archives of Nepal and served on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica (both attested 2018).

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his degrees, including a doctorate, at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).
Kumja Paik Kim (born 1934) works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She received her doctorate from Stanford University and became curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum in 1989.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay and served as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua University and earned his doctorate at Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Academia Sinica, University of Washington (from 1951), and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).
